why: The OpenAI manuscript (recorded twice: openai-2026-eg-counterexample and openai-math-249 are the same event, given identical answers) exhibits a finitely generated group with integral cd 2 and gd 3; one such group refutes the universal statement, so scope is whole and the explicit group is a counterexample. Integral cd is the standard reading of the unqualified statement. No named human has worked through it; the Lean Comparator check uses OpenAI's own definitions and is not digestion (F7), so unreviewed. Credible rather than doubtful: the group is the Bestvina–Brady kernel experts named as the likeliest candidate, the argument is detailed, and no specific error is identified; the sibling withdrawals in the release concern other manuscripts. AI role is generated on the repository's attribution, with this manuscript not listed as an exception. Pasku 2021 explicitly claims EG false (whole) but carries several F10 signals together and is set aside; Kawauchi proves a different conjecture and never claims EG, so variant and also not credible. Bredon/family results are variants; the 1957 and 1997 papers, conditional results and the formal-statement issue bear on the problem without settling cd-2 cases, so none. Revisions of Kawauchi (2024) and Pasku (2026) show no identified new mathematics and keep their original pre-snapshot dates.
doubts: The AI attribution for the EG manuscript rests on a repository-wide sentence, not a per-manuscript statement; the manuscript names no model or human role. Lean definitions are repository-local and unaudited against standard notions. openai-2026-eg-counterexample and openai-math-249 duplicate one event. Whether the counterexample survives expert reading is unknown as of 8 days after posting.
